newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil electronics sales seen up 15 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Brazil electronics sales seen up 15 pct in 1997.

text.p: Brazil's electrical and electronic equipment sales are expected to rise as much as 15 percent next year, Brazil's Electrical and Electronic Industry Association (Abinee) said Thursday.
Sales this year are projected at $34.4 billion, a 22 percent increase from the previous year, Abinee President Nelson Freitas said at a news conference.
Telecommunications equipment and appliance sales should show the strongest growth, expanding by 15 to 20 percent and 15 percent, respectively, he said.
Telecommunications equipment sales should benefit next year from the opening of cellular telephone services to private investment, said Roberto Isnard, head of Abinee's telecom department.
Telecommunications equipment sales should reach $3.6 billion, 48 percent higher than 1995 sales, he said.
"Depending on the pace of privatization next year, the private sector could invest up to $3 billion in the cellular telephone system in Brazil," said Isnard.
He added that investments by state-owned Telebras would reach $8 billion in 1997.
Freitas said the electrical appliance sector would continue to benefit from a boom in consumption that began after the government implemented its anti-inflation plan in mid-1994.
Computer and electronic component sales are expected to rise 10 percent next year, he added.
In 1996, appliance sales are likely to reach $12.9 billion, while computer sales should reach $7.5 billion, Freitas said.
